skill.name: docstring
skill.description: Write and update PyTorch docstrings using project conventions for reStructuredText, Sphinx references, tensor shapes, arguments, returns, warnings, and examples.
skill.summary: Create consistent PyTorch docstrings for Python, C-bound, in-place, and alias APIs.
skill.author: pytorch

static_findings.snippet: This skill describes how to write docstrings for functions and methods in the PyTorch project, follo
- Use **raw strings** (`r"""..."""`) for all docstrings to avoid issues with LaTeX/math backslashes
- Show positional and keyword-only arguments (use `*` separator)
- The `~` prefix shows only the last component (e.g., `Conv2d` instead of `torch.nn.Conv2d`)
See :class:`~torch.nn.Conv2d` for details and output shape.
:func:`new_tensor` always copies :attr:`data`. If you have a Tensor
``data`` and want to avoid a copy, use :func:`torch.Tensor.requires_grad_`
input (Tensor): input tensor of shape :math:`(\text{minibatch} , \text{in\_channels} , iH , iW)`
weight (Tensor): filters of shape :math:`(\text{out\_channels} , kH , kW)`
bias (Tensor, optional): optional bias tensor of shape :math:`(\text{out\_channels})`. Default: ``No
- Type in parentheses: `(Type)`, `(Type, optional)` for optional parameters
- For optional parameters, include "Default: ``value``" at the end
- Use double backticks for inline code: ``` ``None`` ```
dtype (:class:`torch.dtype`, optional): the desired type of returned tensor.
Default: if None, same :class:`torch.dtype` as this tensor.
device (:class:`torch.device`, optional): the desired device of returned tensor.
Default: if None, same :class:`torch.device` as this tensor.
Tensor: Sampled tensor of same shape as `logits` from the Gumbel-Softmax distribution.
If ``hard=True``, the returned samples will be one-hot, otherwise they will
be probability distributions that sum to 1 across `dim`.
- Show actual output when it helps understanding (indent without `>>>`)

content.user_title: Write PyTorch Docstrings with Project Conventions
content.value_statement: PyTorch docstrings require precise reStructuredText, tensor notation, and project conventions. This skill guides consistent signatures, arguments, cross-references, formulas, warnings, and examples.
actual_capabilities: Structures PyTorch docstrings with signatures, summaries, arguments, returns, notes, warnings, and examples.
Formats tensor shapes and equations with Sphinx math directives and inline math roles.
Creates Sphinx cross-references for classes, functions, methods, attributes, and internal labels.
Documents parameter types, optional values, defaults, continuation lines, and return behavior.
Provides patterns for native Python, C-bound, in-place, and alias functions.
Applies PyTorch conventions for examples, external references, reusable arguments, and inserted notes.
limitations: The skill provides guidance only and does not run code or build documentation.
Its conventions target PyTorch and may not match other Python projects.
It cannot infer undocumented behavior without implementation details or authoritative context.
Generated examples, shapes, defaults, and references still require technical verification.

use_cases.title: Document a New PyTorch API
use_cases.description: Create a complete project-style docstring for a new tensor function or method.

use_cases.title: Standardize Existing Documentation
use_cases.description: Update inconsistent docstrings with accurate sections, formatting, references, and examples.

use_cases.title: Review Documentation Changes
use_cases.description: Check proposed docstrings against PyTorch structure, syntax, and consistency expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Write a Basic Docstring
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a PyTorch-style docstring for this function: {function}. Include the signature, a brief description, Args, Returns, and one example.
prompt_templates.scenario: Creating documentation for a straightforward function

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Docstring
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this docstring to follow PyTorch reStructuredText conventions: {docstring}. Preserve behavior and add accurate types, defaults, and Sphinx cross-references.

prompt_templates.title: Document Tensor Semantics
prompt_templates.prompt: Document this tensor operation: {implementation}. Include shape notation, applicable math, edge-case warnings, return details, and executable-style examples.

prompt_templates.title: Align Related APIs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these related APIs and produce consistent PyTorch docstrings: {apis}. Handle native, C-bound, in-place, and alias variants appropriately.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinating documentation across an API family

output_examples.input: Document a tensor normalization function with input, dimension, epsilon, and return value.
output_examples.output: A PyTorch-style docstring with the signature, behavior summary, typed arguments, defaults, return shape, Sphinx references, and an example.

output_examples.input: Improve an existing convolution docstring that lacks shape details and warnings.
output_examples.output: A revised docstring with LaTeX tensor shapes, accurate defaults, cross-references, an important caveat, and a focused usage example.

output_examples.input: Document native, in-place, and alias variants of one operation.
output_examples.output: Consistent entries where the native function is complete, the in-place variant references its method, and the alias points to the original function.

best_practices: Provide the implementation, signature, defaults, and expected tensor shapes before requesting a docstring.
Verify examples, cross-references, formulas, and behavioral claims against the current PyTorch source.
Use raw docstrings and preserve consistent reStructuredText indentation and inline markup.
anti_patterns: Do not invent parameter behavior, return shapes, defaults, or supported data types.
Do not copy generic Python docstring formats that conflict with PyTorch conventions.
Do not add long examples or repeated explanations that obscure the API contract.

faq.question: Is this skill only for PyTorch?
faq.answer: Yes. Its rules and examples target PyTorch documentation, although some reStructuredText practices may transfer to similar projects.

faq.question: Does the skill execute code?
faq.answer: No. It provides writing guidance and examples but does not run code, build documentation, or validate outputs.

faq.question: Can it document C-bound functions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for docstrings attached through PyTorch documentation helpers.

faq.question: Does it support mathematical notation?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Sphinx math directives, inline math roles, and tensor shape notation.

faq.question: Can it handle in-place and alias operations?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends concise references to the original method or function for these variants.

faq.question: What should I verify after generation?
faq.answer: Verify behavior, types, defaults, shapes, formulas, links, cross-references, and example results against current source code.
